sections.heading: 1. Task team and appointment
sections.guidance: The task team this plan belongs to, its lead, the appointment it answers (BEP section 2), and the information manager it reports to.

sections.heading: 2. Deliverables
sections.guidance: One line per information container the task team will deliver: the container name as the naming standard writes it (Settings ▸ Standards in force ▸ naming), its purpose, the level of information need it is produced to (LOIN, BEP section 7), the author and the checker.

sections.heading: 3. Milestones and dates
sections.guidance: For each deliverable: the information exchange it serves, the delivery milestone from the MIDP (the project's programme against the MIDP shows each container ready, late or at risk), and the planned date.

sections.heading: 4. Dependencies and predecessors
sections.guidance: What each deliverable needs from other task teams first (references, federated models, decisions), and when.

sections.heading: 5. Review and authorisation
sections.guidance: Who checks, reviews and authorises each container before it is shared or published — the project's review chain (review@n) names the steps; a container passes the delivery gate (naming, IDS, contract) before any human review.

sections.heading: 6. Resources and capability
sections.guidance: People, software (BEP section 9) and time the task team commits; any capability gap and how it is closed.

sections.heading: 7. Change
sections.guidance: How the plan changes when the MIDP or the appointment changes; who approves a change to a deliverable or a date.
